published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'Since the ACA observations do not show any quiescent excess emission, we conclude that there is no need to invoke the presence of a dust belt at 1-4 AU. We also posit that the slight excess flux density of 101+-9 uJy observed in the 12-m observations compared to the photospheric flux density of 74+-4 uJy extrapolated from infrared wavelengths may be due to coronal heating from continual smaller flares ... If this is true, then the need for warm dust at ~0.4 AU is also removed.' Sec 4.2 (p.6): 'It is clear from our analysis that the entirety of the 1.3 mm emission detected by the ACA results from the short duration stellar flare. No emission is detected above a 3 sigma level during quiescence ... When averaged together with the remaining ~19 hours of non-detections, this transient event appeared as the ~340 uJy source detected by Anglada et al. (2017). Without the detection of a quiescent excess, there is no need to posit the cold belt at 1-4 AU.' ... 'Given the differential source counts at 1.3 mm, the number of sources with flux density > 150 uJy that are expected within the ACA primary beam (FWHM ~39") is 13+10-8, a not insignificant number. In addition, Proxima Centauri sits close to the Galactic plane (latitude -2 deg) in a region of high background cirrus.' Sec 5 (p.7): 'the detection of a flare does not immediately impact the claim of an outer belt at ~30 AU, [but] the significant number of background sources expected in the image and known high level of background cirrus suggest that caution should be used in over-interpreting this marginal result.' Sec 1 (p.1): 'Late M-type stars ... have long pre-main sequence phases during which the stellar luminosity can change significantly'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (data): the 2017 Jan 21 - Apr 25 ALMA 12-m (2 SBs, 41 antennas) and ACA (13 SBs, 8-11 7-m antennas) Band 6 data of programme 2016.A.00013.S, the same data Anglada et al. 2017 used; nothing new observed.

H2 (sensitivity): 'no quiescent excess' is at the ACA sensitivity: first-12 image rms 68 uJy/beam, no source > 3 sigma, a ~2 sigma central peak; 30-s binning for short flares (p.3). A quiescent point source of ~100 uJy 'would not have been detected' (p.3).
H3 (parsimony, not exclusion): the belt conclusion is 'no need to posit/invoke' -- the evidence for the 1-4 au belt is removed; the paper does not claim to exclude a belt below its sensitivity.
H4 (photosphere): 74+-4 uJy at 1.3 mm is an extrapolation of the Ribas et al. 2017 SED model, not a measurement.

H5 (conditional, coronal): the 12-m ~30 uJy excess 'may be' / 'could also be plausibly explained by' / is 'likely' due to continual small flares (by analogy with AU Mic); warm dust at 0.4 au is removed only 'if this is true'.

H6 (background): the 13+10-8 figure uses 1.3 mm differential counts (Carniani et al. 2015, agreeing with Shimizu 2012 and Cai 2013 simulations) over 'the ACA primary beam (FWHM ~39")'; the integration area and formula are not stated. A second, unquantified contamination source is Galactic: latitude -2 deg, high cirrus.
H7 (outer belt): the ACA visibilities 'do not adequately cover the short spatial frequencies needed to measure the total disk flux density'; the flare 'does not immediately impact' the 30 au claim.
hypothesis_drift: STRENGTHENED (the load-bearing drift): formation.py:288-289 'THE 1-4 au BELT, which would have held small primitive bodies, IS WITHDRAWN'; formation.py:43-44 and :410 'MacGregor 2018 withdraws Anglada 2017's 1-4 au belt'; formation.py:458 SURVEY_BELT_1_4AU_WITHDRAWN_BY_SOURCE = True. The source says 'no need to posit' (p.6) / 'no need to invoke' (p.1, p.7): the EVIDENCE is removed (H3). Computed here: the first-12 ACA image disfavours star + Anglada's ~200 uJy belt at ~2.0 sigma and Anglada's full 340 uJy at ~3.0 sigma; a belt fainter than ~130 uJy (2 sigma of the 68 uJy rms) is not excluded, and such a belt could still hold small bodies. 'Withdraws' also names an author act; MacGregor et al. are not the Anglada et al. authors, and the one discover_papers call found no Anglada response (absence of a find, not a finding). The tree's own quote at :286-287 is verbatim-correct; the drift is in the gloss.

rederivation.outcome: 6 AGREES, 7 MEASURED, 4 DISCREPANCY, 1 NARROWS. Six results AGREE: flare fluence to final-obs flux (1.16-1.57 vs 1.17+-0.10 mJy); image-weighted dilution to the 334 uJy combined source (199-312, within 1 sigma); 12-m excess ~30 uJy (27+-9.8); peak L_nu 2.02e14; the solar 2e13 and 10x ratio; delta = 3.32. MEASURED (computed from inputs, no published counterpart): the first-12 data disfavour star + A17's belt at 2.0 sigma (A17 total 3.0 sigma), and 'no belt' fits at +0.5 sigma; background counts in five candidate areas (the MEASURED rows). The NARROWS row: 'no need to posit' is evidence removal, not exclusion. The four DISCREPANCIES, all recorded and none refuting: (i) the rms quotes 47/68/150 are mutually inconsistent; (ii) the 1e21 erg/s quiescent luminosity has an unstated band; (iii) sigma_delta 0.83 vs 0.50; (iv) the 13+10-8 background figure is NOT REPRODUCED under the literal FWHM-beam area (~1.6 from the counts M18 cites) and lies within its own error only if the area runs to the ~46" first null. Only (iv) touches a number the tree quotes; none moves a tree conclusion.

later_literature.ref: Burton, MacGregor, Osten et al. 2025, arXiv:2503.21890 (ApJ, 'The Proxima Centauri Campaign -- first constraints on millimeter flare rates from ALMA')
later_literature.what: About 50 h of ALMA 1.3 mm data (2017, 2019, 2021), 463 flares. The 2017 Mar 24 flare is independently recovered at 119+-7 mJy with t_1/2 ~ 15 s, so the flare attribution of the ACA excess is confirmed. It also finds >= 8 sigma short flares in the 2017 ACA data on 1 Feb and 19 Mar, inside M18's 'first 12' set, which M18's 30-s binning could not see. That narrows M18's p.3 'no sources above 3 sigma ... in any of the first 12' to 'at 30-s binning' and strengthens the flare picture. alpha_FFD = 2.92: small flares dominate, consistent with the coronal reading of the 12-m excess. The pages read do not revisit the dust belts.

The count source M18 cites. Its 1.3 mm Schechter fit (phi* = 1.8e3 deg^-2, S* = 1.7 mJy, alpha = -2.08) gives N(>150 uJy) = 1.74e4 deg^-2, about 1.6 sources in the ACA FWHM disk against M18's 13. M18's figure is reproduced only with an area out to about the first null.

later_literature.ref: Gonzalez-Lopez et al. 2020, arXiv:2002.07199 (ASPECS 1.2 mm counts)
later_literature.what: Later and deeper counts: N(>=158 uJy at 1.2 mm) = 1.06e4 deg^-2, i.e. N(>150 uJy at 1.3 mm) ~ 1.07e4. That lowers the background expectation further (1.0 in the FWHM disk). The 30 au belt stays marginal regardless.

The claim M18 re-analyses. It gives the cold belt ~200 uJy of a ~270 uJy excess (Sec 3.2), a marginal 30 au belt of ~1.7 mJy (Sec 3.3), ACA primary-beam FWHM ~39" with first null ~46" (Sec 2), and an Fig 1 extent of PB > 20%. It supplies the inputs to the ~2 sigma belt test and the area options in rederive items 3 and 7.

lacked_data: What M18 had: exactly A17's data (H1). M18 needed no new data, only a time-resolved re-analysis, and A17 had the same visibilities without looking at them in time. What M18 lacked, and what came later: (1) the mm flare rate. B25 (2025, ~50 h, 463 flares) measured it; flares are common, and the Mar 24 event is recovered independently at 119+-7 mJy. This CONFIRMS the flare attribution. (2) Second-scale time resolution in the 'quiescent' 2017 ACA sets. B25 finds >= 8 sigma short flares on 1 Feb and 19 Mar 2017, inside M18's first 12 observations. This narrows M18's 'no source above 3 sigma' to its 30-s binning, and it strengthens rather than weakens 'no quiescent excess'. (3) A direct 1.3 mm photospheric measurement is still lacking: 74+-4 uJy remains an SED extrapolation, so the 12-m ~30 uJy excess and its coronal reading stay conditional, exactly as M18 and the tree both say. (4) Deeper source counts: ASPECS 2020 lowers the expected background below the Carniani 2015 level, and M18's 13+10-8 is not reproduced from either under the literal beam reading. That moves a number the tree quotes, not the tree's conclusion. (5) Deep data on the 30 au belt: the 2019 ACA campaign (34 h on source, B25 Table 1) exists, but no dust analysis of it was found or read here, so it is OPEN whether it confirms or refutes the outer belt. Net: M's hypothesis is tested and does NOT move this result's conclusions. The later data reinforce the flare attribution. The one place the tree overreads is its own gloss 'WITHDRAWN', which the data at hand support only as 'no longer evidenced; disfavoured at ~2 sigma at Anglada's flux'.
grade_evidence: The flare attribution STANDS. It is re-derived here (fluence to 1.17 mJy; image-weighted dilution to 334 uJy) and independently confirmed by Burton et al. 2025 (READ). The 12-m coronal conditional and the PMS sentence are carried faithfully. The grade is NARROWED because the tree's gloss is stronger than the source on the one conjunct it banks. formation.py:288-289 / :43-44 / :410 / :458 read 'THE 1-4 au BELT ... IS WITHDRAWN' and 'WITHDRAWN_BY_SOURCE = True'. The source concludes 'no need to posit/invoke' at ACA first-12 sensitivity (rms 68 uJy), and computed here the data disfavour star + A17's ~200 uJy belt at ~2.0 sigma (3.0 sigma at A17's full 340). A fainter belt, which could hold small bodies, is not excluded. The result holds on 'the 1-4 au belt is not evidenced', a smaller claim than 'withdrawn'. Secondary: the 13+10-8 background figure the tree quotes is not reproduced from the counts M18 cites under the literal FWHM-beam area (~1.6; ~1.0 with ASPECS 2020). It fits within its own error only with a first-null area. This is a recorded discrepancy, not WRONG, and the 30 au belt's 'marginal' status does not rest on it. Downstream: D25's verdict (OPEN AND UNCHANGED) and SURVEY_CONFIRMED_RESERVOIR = UNDETERMINED do not move, because an unevidenced belt is not a surveyed reservoir under either reading. Only the wording of the 'WITHDRAWN' flag overstates the source.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree rewords the flag to the source's scope, e.g. 'the 1-4 au belt is no longer evidenced (MacGregor 2018: no need to posit; disfavoured ~2 sigma at A17 flux)'. Or a later READ analysis of deeper data (e.g. the 34 h 2019 ACA campaign) sets an upper limit excluding a 1-4 au belt at the flux that would matter; that would make 'withdrawn' literally true. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a later deep analysis detects a quiescent 1-4 au excess, which would re-open the belt. To WRONG (for the background figure only, which the tree merely quotes): M18's area or method is stated and shown to give ~1-2, not 13. Even then the tree's 'marginal' conclusion survives. Nothing here shows the flare attribution to be wrong.
